story: The Hotel del Coronado, also called The Del, is a beachfront hotel in Coronado, across San Diego Bay from San Diego. It is a rare surviving wooden Victorian beach resort. It became a California Historical Landmark in 1970 and a National Historic Landmark in 1977.

In November 1885 five investors bought Coronado and North Island, about 4,000 acres, for $110,000. E. S. Babcock and Hampton L. Story created the Coronado Beach Company and hired architect James W. Reid. When the hotel opened in 1888, it was the largest resort hotel in the world.
The company also ran ferries, piped fresh water under the bay and built a railroad. The hotel had one of the state's largest electrical power plants, which served the whole town until the 1920s.
stops.fact: It once powered the whole town.
stops.disputed: Many people think a huge old hotel must be brick or stone. Wikipedia says it is wood, the second-largest wooden building in the country.

The hotel is made of brick.
claims.why: It is a wooden Victorian beach resort.

story: Mission Basilica San Diego de Alcalá was the second Franciscan-founded mission in the Californias. Spanish friar Junípero Serra founded it on July 16, 1769, in an area that the Kumeyaay people had long inhabited. It is named for Saint Didacus of Alcalá, known in Spanish as San Diego.

It was the site of the first Christian burial in Alta California. The first mission burned in 1775 during an uprising by local people. Father Luis Jayme, killed in that uprising, lies beneath the chancel floor.
The church standing today was built in the early nineteenth century and is the fifth to stand on this location. The mission site is a National Historic Landmark.
stops.fact: The church today is the fifth on this spot.
stops.disputed: Many people think the old church we see is the first. Wikipedia says it is the fifth to stand here.

The church standing today is the first one built here.

story: Balboa Park is a 1,200-acre historic park in San Diego. It hosted the 1915 to 1916 Panama-California Exposition and the 1935 to 1936 California Pacific International Exposition, and both left landmark buildings behind. The park was named a National Historic Landmark District in 1977.

The Botanical Building was built for the first exposition and remains one of the largest lath structures in the world. Alfred D. Robinson, founder of the San Diego Floral Society, suggested a lath house for the fair. A garden and lily pond were built in front of it in 1915.
During World War I and World War II the navy used the pond for swimming lessons. The building closed in 2021 for renovations and reopened in December 2024.

story: The Casa de Estudillo was built in 1827 by José María Estudillo and his son José Antonio Estudillo, early settlers of San Diego. It was considered one of the finest houses in Mexican California. It stands in Old Town San Diego State Historic Park and is a National and California Historical Landmark.

The Spanish Colonial house is U-shaped, 113 feet across the front and 98 feet along each wing. Its 13 rooms connect only through a covered outdoor walkway, not inside halls. A cupola on top gave a view of the plaza for bullfights and festivals.

José Antonio died in 1852, and the family stayed until 1887. Helen Hunt Jackson's 1884 novel Ramona made Californio life famous nationwide, and the house became linked with the story. Old postcards called it Ramona's Marriage Place. A restoration in 1910 removed some walls to enlarge the chapel and schoolroom.
stops.fact: The rooms connect only through an outdoor walkway.
stops.disputed: Many people think the house was built for the novel. Wikipedia says it was built in 1827, and the novel came out in 1884.

claims.t: The Casa de Estudillo was built in 1827.
The house was built for the novel Ramona.
claims.why: The house dates to 1827. The novel was published in 1884.
